1. The fundamentals: Finn Jacobsen’s Fundamentals of General Linear Acoustics

It doesn’t just give you bullet points. It explains the fundamentals and basic phenomena of acoustics in detail, with examples and plenty of figures, and a lot of concepts I had only half understood became clear after reading it.

The book came out in 2013 and not many people know it. Beranek and Kuttruff have both written introductory acoustics books too, but to me neither is as intuitive or as thorough as Jacobsen’s, though they make good companions to it. Sadly, Professor Jacobsen died a couple of years ago, far too young.

Other areas:

  • Room acoustics: Kuttruff’s Room Acoustics
  • Psychoacoustics: Zwicker’s Psychoacoustics
  • Virtual acoustics and auralization: Vorländer’s Auralization
  • Soundscape: Professor Jian Kang’s Soundscape
  • Beamforming: Van Trees’s Optimum Array Processing, and Johnson’s Array Signal Processing
  • Nearfield acoustical holography (NAH): Williams’s Fourier Acoustics
  • Binaural technology and spatial hearing: Blauert’s Spatial Hearing, and Head-Related Transfer Function and Virtual Auditory Display by Professor Bosun Xie of South China University of Technology
  • Railway noise: Thompson’s Railway Noise and Vibration
  • Noise and vibration: Fahy’s Fundamentals of Sound and Vibration
  • Acoustic theory in depth: Morse’s Theoretical Acoustics (there is a Chinese translation)
  • Handbooks: the Springer Handbook of Acoustics

For more on acoustics (popular science, curiosities, little-known facts, industrial applications and where the field is heading), see my Zhihu column Acoustics: Tech You Can Hear and my WeChat Official Account, Ziyu Acoustics.
